idea_name: A/D extrema trend-line crossover as leading price-breakout sensor
mechanism: Fill TempIND[] with iAD(sy,tf,j) over nBars; detect troughs/peaks from bar 2; build global up/down trend lines by connecting the leftmost qualifying min/max to a main extremum at index pbar=2 after virtual-line scan removes intermediate piercers via EquationDirect; project the line onto bars 1 and 2; if A/D[1] vs A/D[2] straddles the projected levels, emit CrossGDN/CrossGUP (+1 buy / -1 sell). Optional local two-extrema lines and with-trend crosses (add).
data_needed: iAD series for symbol/TF; nBars extrema window (e.g. 30–250); EquationDirect line projection; NormalizeDouble compare on bars 1–2
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol/TF via SignalCrossIND(sy,tf); tested EURUSD M5, nBars=250, 2009–2010
why_new_for_mis: Turns Accumulation/Distribution into an explicit leading change sensor: A/D trend-line break is treated as a probabilistic precursor of price trend-line break, with global vs local scale and direction-coded returns usable as MIS regime-change features.
quote: It is known that the Accumulation/Distribution A/D Indicator has one interesting feature - a breakout of the trend line plotted in this indicator chart suggests, with a certain degree of probability, a forthcoming breakout of the trend line in the price chart

idea_name: Weighted global+local A/D crossover combination codes
mechanism: Independently flag CrossGUP/CrossGDN on global A/D trend lines and CrossUP/CrossDN on local last-two-extrema lines; optionally return combined weights (11/-11 both scales, 10/-10 global only, 1/-1 local only) so callers can require dual-scale confirmation before acting.
data_needed: Same A/D extrema arrays; local=true; dual crossover flags
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same any-symbol/TF A/D function; local extrema on rightmost peaks/troughs
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a multi-horizon change feature (slow global vs fast local volume-flow structure) with explicit concurrence codes rather than a single binary cross.
quote: You can also combine signals of crossovers of "global" and "local" trends in the A/D chart

idea_name: A/D volume-flow path as liquidity accumulation substrate
mechanism: Use the full A/D line (iAD) as the sensing series whose extrema define accumulation vs distribution structure; trend-line geometry on that path encodes whether volume-backed buying/selling pressure is intact or breaking, independent of plotting price trends.
data_needed: iAD(sy,tf,*) history; peak/trough classification on A/D values
why_new_for_mis: Supplies MIS a volume-integrated liquidity/flow state series on which change sensors operate, not just OHLC trend lines.
quote: Trend lines are drawn based on the A/D chart extrema identified whereby an uptrend line connects lower extrema and a downtrend line connects upper extrema.

idea_name: Geometric SL:TP:spread expected win-rate odds sensor
mechanism: Given stop distance, take-profit multiple, and spread, map net pip gain/loss (e.g. SL 8 / TP 12 with 2-pip spread for a 10:10 intended RR) and set P(TP)=1-(TP_dist/(SL_dist+TP_dist)); use this geometric prior as the baseline win chance under random price landing.
data_needed: StopLoss decimal, Risk:Reward ratio, Spread decimal
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Excel sandbox; 4/5-digit FX (not JPY); abstract random-walk market
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an instrument-agnostic odds feature from trade geometry alone, useful as a null model against which empirical hit rates are compared.
quote: Given an even chance of the price "landing" at any point in that range, then the chance of hitting the take profit is: 1- (12 / (8+12)) = 0.4 = 40%

idea_name: Matched-SL:TP random-entry control for edge attribution
mechanism: Run a Random EA that opens long/short at random on bar open with the same SL/TP distances and lot rules as the candidate strategy over the same history; if performances are similar, attribute profitability to SL:TP geometry interacting with the period’s trend rather than to entry logic.
data_needed: Backtest history window; matched SL/TP points; static or %-risk lots; OptimizationNumber for multi-pass
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Random EA backtests any symbol/TF; notes multi-year bull trends skewing TP>SL systems
why_new_for_mis: Provides a MIS diagnostic sensor that flags when a history window’s directional regime makes naive SL:TP ratios look like alpha.
quote: If you test the performance of an EA over the same history period against a randomly trading EA (with the same SL:TP ratios and lot size rules), and the performances are similar, then that may tell you something interesting about your strategy.

idea_name: Polynomial regression close-path extrapolator via matrix normal equations
mechanism: On user-selected close sample (x=index,y=close), build Vandermonde-style normal matrix A[i][j]=mean(x^(i+j)) and RHS B[i]=mean(y*x^i); solve with MatrGJBatchSolve for coefficients of degree polyDegree; evaluate the polynomial on the in-sample interval and to the right of it as an extrapolated directional path.
data_needed: Close series on selected chart interval; polyDegree < numPoints-1; LibMatrix Gauss-Jordan solve
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart candlestick closes; interval set by two vertical lines; extrapolation to a third line
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a classical sequence smoother/forecaster: local polynomial state of the close path plus an explicit right-edge extrapolation usable as a short-horizon directional feature.
quote: Polynomial values on the extrapolation interval can be used to predict the direction of the price movement.

idea_name: Cross-TF concurrence count as stronger change alert
mechanism: Sum process() hits across the TF cascade for one symbol into Total; if Total>1 fire a Warning Alert that the same instrument has UserText crosses on multiple timeframes simultaneously.
data_needed: Per-TF crossover returns; Total accumulator per symbol
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same multi-symbol .set list; current chart TF sets the top of the cascade
why_new_for_mis: Turns isolated TF crosses into a multi-horizon concurrence feature—stronger regime-change evidence when several clocks agree.
